nodes.subject: long-term HHKB owner
nodes.object: Fn-layer arrows became muscle memory over more than ten years, while modifier placement and layout changes can still make shortcuts uncomfortable.

support_spans.exact_quote: Background: I'm a programmer and have been on HHKB for a bit over 10 years.

So moving around using arrows are just natural to me: just add left thumb, I feel right home. It's also super easy to do ctrl+arrows & ctrl+shift+arrows to move around words and select words, it's super convenient.
But now to use CMD, I had to twist my arm to use the thumb to reach it or use my palm to press it down, it gets very uncomfortable over time.

nodes.subject: compact-keyboard advice discussion
nodes.object: One buyer explicitly rejects 60 percent because they want arrow keys, and a commenter suggests 75 percent as a more compact dedicated-arrow alternative to TKL.

support_spans.exact_quote: I decided to go with a TKL keyboard, NOT 60%. I want extra arrow keys.

I don't have enough knowledge to answer your questions but looking at your size comments, I would suggest you to consider 75% keyboards too, as you mention that you want the arrow keys and they are slightly more compact than a TKL keyboard.

nodes.subject: Feker Alice 80 owner
nodes.object: The board is heavy, not seen as portable, difficult to fit in a portable case, and requires a manual for unlabeled secondary functions.

support_spans.exact_quote: But it is also pretty heavy and so I don't see it being portable at all outside of the house. Also it is difficult to fit into a portable case.
There are no secondary labeling on the keys, like for bluetooth pairing or to explain anything. So you need to use the manual for reference.

nodes.subject: wireless Corne discussion
nodes.object: A small-battery build lasted less than a day, while comments attribute large runtime differences to OLEDs, LEDs, display choice, and battery capacity.

support_spans.exact_quote: Right now I am using 2x 100max batteries. The life time is really poor - not even a day. Oleds are enabled, rgba is disabled.
If you have the RGBs soldered, and external VCC on, they are drawing roughly 7-8mAh per LED in standby keeping the communication on. And as said OLEDs are also a battery killer.
I have 600mah in my build and the central half gets roughly two months on one charge, no displays

nodes.subject: Arrow keys article
nodes.object: Arrow keys are navigation keys commonly used for caret movement, scrolling, selection, and other software actions.

support_spans.exact_quote: The arrow keys have a wide variety of functions. In a command-line interface (CLI), text box , or word processor , they typically enable caret navigation , allowing the user to move the text cursor between characters and lines.
Moving text cursor to the right, left, previous line and next line

nodes.subject: Keyboard layout article
nodes.object: Physical, visual, and functional layouts differ, and software mapping determines the response to a key press and can be changed or extended.

support_spans.exact_quote: A keyboard layout is any specific physical, visual, or functional arrangement of the keys, legends, or key-meaning associations (respectively) of a computer keyboard , mobile phone , or other computer-controlled typographic keyboard.

Functional layout is the arrangement of the key-meaning association or keyboard mapping , determined in software, of all the keys of a keyboard; it is this (rather than the legends) that determines the actual response to a key press.
Often, [ a ] a user can change keyboard mapping in system settings. In addition, software may be available to modify or extend keyboard functionality.

nodes.subject: Bluetooth article
nodes.object: Bluetooth is a short-range packet radio and wire-replacement protocol used for low-bandwidth keyboard communication.

support_spans.exact_quote: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology standard that is used for exchanging data between fixed and mobile devices over short distances and building personal area networks (PANs).
Uses Bluetooth is a standard wire-replacement communications protocol primarily designed for low power consumption, with a short range based on low-cost transceiver microchips in each device.
Wireless communication with PC input and output devices, the most common being the mouse , keyboard and printer .

nodes.subject: Bluetooth keyboard communication

accepted_phrases: Bluetooth is a short-range low-power wire-replacement protocol used by keyboards, but the generic description supplies no product-specific end-to-end latency or perceptibility result for the three candidates.

nodes.subject: frozen compact-keyboard matrix
nodes.object: K12 offers a 60 percent hot-swappable Bluetooth and wired route with Fn-layer arrows and conditional 240-hour wording. K6 is cheaper and provides a 65 percent layout, dedicated arrows, Bluetooth and wired modes, dimensions, and conflicting conditional runtime wording. MX Keys Mini is thinner and lighter with conditional battery wording but has a 52/100 display and no captured wired-input statement.

nodes.subject: compact marketing and commute fit
nodes.object: Stated dimensions and weight can bound physical fit, but package measurements must not be substituted for product measurements. The Feker report shows why heft, case fit, and access to secondary functions matter without measuring any candidate, so a real bag, table, shortcut, and carrying trial remains required.

nodes.subject: dedicated versus layered arrow access
nodes.object: Arrow navigation is a real workflow need, software mappings can change functions, and a long-term HHKB owner shows layers can become natural. Another buyer rejects 60 percent for arrows. Because this commuter explicitly relies on arrows and shortcuts and fears layer gymnastics, K6 dedicated arrows satisfy the stated fit better than K12 Fn-layer access unless a trial reverses that preference.

nodes.subject: wireless battery evidence
nodes.object: K12 and MX Keys Mini runtime statements depend on backlight conditions, while the K6 body contains materially different 10-hour, 72-hour, and nine-day wording. Corne anecdotes show that LEDs, displays, battery size, and configuration alter runtime. Therefore all product runtimes remain conditional seller claims and the unrelated Corne numbers cannot be transferred.

nodes.subject: Bluetooth convenience and typing latency
nodes.object: Bluetooth supports short-range low-bandwidth keyboard links, but neither the generic mechanism nor the three product bodies measures end-to-end latency or perceptibility. Bluetooth 5.1 and Low Energy labels therefore do not settle lag. Explicit wired keyboard input on K12 and K6 is a fallback under uncertainty; MX Keys Mini's USB-C charging wording is not promoted to wired input.
